Our first look at Diablo 4's Warlock and the game's next season arrive in today's livestream - watch it here

📅 05 Mar 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (285 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Vg247

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Diablo 4’s next, long-awaited Developer Update finally airs today.
  • Industry observers note that the Warlock’s initial unveiling, however, was incredibly brief, showing no gameplay.
  • Blizzard is bringing back its Developer Update livestream programme, which is the more structured, information-dense series of developer showcases.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Diablo 4’s next, long-awaited Developer Update finally airs today. This meaty livestream was first revealed nearly a month ago, when Blizzard initially revealed that the game’s next class is the Warlock.

Industry observers note that the Warlock’s initial unveiling, however, was incredibly brief, showing no gameplay. It also didn't explain how the class is going to fit within the existing roster. This all changes today.

Blizzard is bringing back its Developer Update livestream programme, which is the more structured, information-dense series of developer showcases. The focus of this one, of course, is going to mainly be on the Warlock class.

It has been revealed that the Warlock is one of two classes coming to Diablo 4 with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion. The first, the Paladin, is already available in the game for anyone who pre-orders the expansion. The Warlock will instead arrive alongside the expansion on April 28.

Sources indicate that the Developer Revision will also include a first look at the game’s next season (Season 12), currently set for March 10. This mini season will only last until the expansion’s release, so it’s going to be interesting to see what it brings to the game.

You’ll be able to watch the showcase live at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 7pm GMT on Diablo 4’s official YouTube, Twitch, and Twitter channels. We’ve embedded the YouTube and Twitch players below for your convenience.

In a recent development, among the topics the Developer Update will cover are the Killstreaks system, as well as Bloodstained items. As always, you can also expect a Q&A segment at the end of the show, and I imagine there’s going to be a few about the Warlock.

Industry News: Treyarch lays off lead Call of Duty writer and Zombies veteran after "approximately 20 years" of service

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (532 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Treyarch's former Senior lead writer, Craig Houston, has been laid off after approximately 20 years of service with the developer.
  • "After approximately 20 years, I was sadly one of those affected by recent layoffs," he noted in his posts.
  • It has been revealed that on Twitter/X, he quote tweeted a video celebrating 30 years of Treyarch and featuring footage from many of the games he worked on to share his message.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Treyarch's former Senior lead writer, Craig Houston, has been laid off after approximately 20 years of service with the developer. In a post made to both his Twitter/X account and LinkedIn, the developer thanked fans for their support during his two decades with the company and confirmed he was impacted by recent reorganistation within the studio.

"After approximately 20 years, I was sadly one of those affected by recent layoffs," he noted in his posts. "I am proud to have worked with so many talented people - many of whom will remain friends for life. Thanks to all the fans for your enthusiasm, support, and kind words over the years.".

It has been revealed that on Twitter/X, he quote tweeted a video celebrating 30 years of Treyarch and featuring footage from many of the games he worked on to share his message. It appears the layoffs referenced are part of the broad reorganistation affecting 3200 jobs that Xbox declared earlier this year. Treyarch, as part of Activision Blizzard, is owned by Xbox.

Recent findings suggest that houston is a bonafide veteran of the esteemed FPS series. His first Call of Duty title at Treyarch was Call of Duty 3, where he worked as a video editor. This was followed by World at War, Black Ops 1 through 4, where he is credited as a writer and designer. For Modern Warfare, Black Ops - Cold War, Vanguard, Modern Warfare 3, then Black Ops 6 and 7, he is listed as a member of the design team and in 'creative development'. He is not credited on this year's Modern Warfare 4.

If you've picked up a Call of Duty game in the past decade-plus, you'll have interacted with Houston's work: he was a central creative force behind the writing for Treyarch's campaign modes since 2006 (with Call of Duty 3) and the main writer for the Zombies mode since 2008 (with Call of Duty: World at War). Alongside Jimmy Zielinski, Jason Blundell, and Kevin Drew, Houston was an integral part of the evolution of the Zombies pillar of Call of Duty, and shaped it into the series-defining thing it is today. There has been a fair amount of community support for Houston since he declared the news yesterday; he was a popular dev, and a lot of the Zombies-specific fan communities online hold a lot of respect for him.

It has been revealed that "Craig is a great guy," notes one user on Reddit. "You can tell how much he loves the story/characters he writes just by how excited he is when he talks about them in promo material.".

In a recent development, "You're a Legend Craig, it was an honor to work with you," says ex-Treyarch vet, Tony Flame, in a reply to Houston's X post. "You created a truly special experience that will live on in the kinds of millions fans. Wishing you the best [...].".

From all of us here at Eurogamer, and myself personally - who really admires the character-work and emergent storytelling present in the Xbox 360-era Call of Duty games, specifically - we wish you the best and good luck with the future, Craig.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that look at you, you lucky devil, you're being treated to a new Warhammer 40,000: Darktide class next month!
  • According to a blog post accompanying the reveal of the class, the Sisters Novitiate work a tad differently compared to other classes available in the game.
  • You build up their Faith while fighting, in turn choosing from a selection of doctrines and pledges in their talent tree, "each shaping how Faith is both accumulated and put to use.

It has been revealed that look at you, you lucky devil, you're being treated to a new Warhammer 40,000: Darktide class next month! This class is called the Sisters Novitiate, a group of wonderfully violent women with a penchant for crossbows, burning people alive and putting a stop to anyone that dares to oppose the God-Emperor. Neato!

According to a blog post accompanying the reveal of the class, the Sisters Novitiate work a tad differently compared to other classes available in the game. "Unlike other classes, the Sisters Novitiate are able to choose from six divine and devastating Acts of Faith, as opposed to blitz and combat abilities," the post explains. "Their abilities draw upon reserves of Faith, allowing them to unleash brutal Neural Whip attacks to the inspiring Icon of Purity and protective prayers. Faith can take many forms for the Sisters Novitiate, each channeling the Emperor's divine will and bringing his wrath upon his enemies.".

You build up their Faith while fighting, in turn choosing from a selection of doctrines and pledges in their talent tree, "each shaping how Faith is both accumulated and put to use. Any two Acts of Faith can be equipped at a time, allowing players to choose how their Novitiate will unleash righteous fury on the battlefield." I mentioned crossbows, right? Well, I stand lore corrected, as what they technically have is the Condemnor Stakethrower, which "pins what remains of their enemies to the walls." They do also have access to a flamethrower, a massive ole mace, your classic sword and shield, and whatever the hell a "Penitent Eviscerator.".

This DLC class also comes the same day as a free enhancement, which will introduce the Metlagun, equipable by the Sisters Novitiate as well as the Veteran. Apparently there'll be more information on the free update soon. Oh, and the release date! It's December 7th, so a little under a month away. I'm sure you can (Dark)tide over the next few weeks by rewatching the gnarly reveal trailer.

After weeks of Marvel's Countdown to Avengers: Doomsday podcast airing on Disney Plus, Marvel fans have started to theorize that host and Ms. Marvel star Iman Vellani may actually be in the upcoming movie, and the evidence is hiding in plain sight.

Industry observers note that one fan posted a screenshot of the podcast over on Reddit, pointing out that Vellani is sitting on a black director's chair in every episode. Why is that important? Well, you may remember that rather lengthy Avengers: Doomsday casting announcement, which was live-streamed on Instagram, which revealed the bulk of the cast by panning over to directors' chairs with names printed on them.

Now fans think that Vellani is going to turn her chair around and reveal her casting in the final episode of Countdown to Doomsday. "So this is obviously Iman's Doomsday chair and she will reveal it in the last episode, right?" said the original Reddit poster. You may be thinking why this theory has only just started to heat up when the podcast has been airing since August. But now that it has been confirmed that Hailee Steinfeld will return as Kate Bishop, Vellani's casting seems even more likely.

It has been revealed that "Kathryn Newton revealed her own chair after she appeared in the first trailer, then when the ScreenX version of the trailer dropped, we noticed that Scott and Cassie's meeting was happening at Kate Bishop's apartment, and now Hailee Steinfeld revealed her chair before the next trailer, which comes out in a few hours," stated the fan. "Since Kamala is the one who brought these characters together to form her fresh team, Kamala is definitely in that apartment with them, right?".

Industry observers note that the plot thickens as back in April 2026, Lord of the Rings star Andy Serkis seemingly let Vellani's casting slip. When the Ms. Marvel star told Serkis that she is excited to see The Hunt for Gollum, Serkis replied, "I'm excited to see you in Doomsday." Many passed that off as a joke, but it may not have been. As we know, the full Doomsday cast has yet to be revealed, as co-director Anthony Russo has confirmed that he and Joe Russo still haven't revealed the full cast.

In and amongst all of the GTA 6 news that's been happening this week, Bethesda has made a very quiet announcement about a fresh Fallout-inspired game, and it's one of the most bizarre crossovers we've seen in a while!

Simply put, Xbox and Bethesda are teaming up with the developers behind games such as A Building Full of Cats to create a Wasteland-themed game where you'll seemingly have to locate cats throughout the Fallout universe.

In other words, this would appear to be a hidden object game.

Industry observers note that we'll throw some footage of one of this developer's Xbox titles down below so you can get an idea of what to expect. Their games are also always very inexpensive, and they also have some fantastic reviews on the Xbox Store.

There's obviously lots of other Fallout stuff in the works right now, including two remasters based on Fallout 3 and Fallout: Upcoming Vegas, as well as the much-anticipated Fallout 5. This new "inspired" game clearly just serves as a bit of fun to plug the gap, and we reckon it might actually do very well when it rolls out in the future.

According to recent reports, it's cool to see Xbox partnering on lighthearted ideas like this! Long may it continue - do it with Halo and Gears next?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The big Diablo 4 Developer Revision has indeed delivered the goods.
  • You can tell Blizzard wanted to have a bit of fun with Season of Slaughter, as many of its major features make it look like a limited-time event, but there is plenty to be excited about here.
  • Sources indicate that season of Slaughter kicks off March 11, and will run until the following season kicks off April 28, with the launch of the Lord of Hatred expansion.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The big Diablo 4 Developer Revision has indeed delivered the goods. One of the livestream’s big topics was, of course, the game’s upcoming mini-season, which is set to kick off next week and run until the launch of Lord of Hatred, the game’s anticipated next expansion.

You can tell Blizzard wanted to have a bit of fun with Season of Slaughter, as many of its major features make it look like a limited-time event, but there is plenty to be excited about here.

Sources indicate that season of Slaughter kicks off March 11, and will run until the following season kicks off April 28, with the launch of the Lord of Hatred expansion. Many of the season’s biggest additions were available to preview in the 2.6.0 Public Test Realm.

Recent findings suggest that patch 2.6.0, as you might have guessed, is the one that will kick off the slaughter next week. The headline feature here is ability to become The Butcher, the iconic in-game boss who randomly invades players’ games.

When you play as The Butcher, you’ll be rewarded the more kills you get in quick succession. Your skills hotbar will transform to become something more fitting of The Butcher, making them more brutal. You’ll also earn a seasonal currency as you play.

In a recent development, starting the seasonal questline is how you can begin to assume The Butcher’s form. A Taste of Power can be initiated from Gea Kul. Transforming into The Butcher can be done in a few ways. As you play, you’ll earn Meaty Offerings, which can later be spent on Shrines of Slaughter in the new Helltide. Once activated, the shrine will draw more enemies towards you.

If you never venture into PvP zones in Diablo 4, this season may change your mind. The standard PvP combat that could only be found in Fields of Hatred has been replaced with a Ceremony of Slaughter, a new event that rewards you for killing enemies quickly. See it through and The Butcher’s Idol will spawn, allowing you to transform into it.

Sources indicate that elsewhere in the world, you’ll also be able to attain the same power at Slaughterhouses, a latest activity type available this season. Inside, you immediately become The Butcher for the entirety of the run.

The Butcher’s arrival also ties into two of the other Season of Slaughter’s more interesting additions. First, the Killstreak system finally arrives in Diablo 4, rewarding you for being as efficient as possible in carving your way through enemies.

According to recent reports, anyone who played Diablo 3 should be familiar with how it works. It kicks off the moment you get a kill, and has a visible timer where you’ll need continue performing the same action to up your streak. The more kills you get, the more often your timer will refresh.

There are five tiers to climb through: Killstreak, Carnage, Devastation, Bloodbath, and Massacre. You’re awarded for the tier you manage to reach before the timer runs out. You’ll earn XP and seasonal rep each time a Killstreak is achieved.

The other Butcher-themed addition is Bloodied Items, which is a new item quality available throughout this season. They play into the Killstreak system to grant you even more power. Bloodied Items come with unique affixes that scale off your Killstreak tier. You’ll see many familiar items in that pool, as any item in the game has a chance to drop as Bloodied. Bloodied Items can also be acquired by earning Fresh Meat.

Sources indicate that even if none of that sounds exciting, you’re probably going to redownload the game for The Paladin free trial, which kicks off alongside the latest season on March 11. The trial is only available until March 18, and it lets you try out the Paladin class.

The trial is available across PC, PlayStation, and Xbox. You’ll be able to take the latest class for a spin, but your progress will be capped at level 25. The Paladin can be permanently unlocked by buying the Lord of Hatred expansion, as it’s one of two classes the expansion is introducing.

The good news is that any progress you make in the free trial will carry over to the full game if/when you buy the expansion.

Recent findings suggest that season of Slaughter also kicks off a Doom: The Dark Ages collaboration event. As we’ve come to expect, there’s a very limited free component to the collaboration, in the form of the Doom Reliquary. This is essentially a mini-battle pass that includes the Shield Saw skin, Slayer’s Flair, the head of the Cyberdemon as a back trophy and various other smaller bits.

It has been revealed that the more impressive items - such as character skins, will instead be available to purchase for real money. The list includes the Doom Slayer armor, Mecha Dragon Serrat skin for your cat mount, and a Cacodemon pet.

Though the armor skin is cross-class compatible, judging by how much previous collaboration items have cost in Diablo 4, most of us probably won’t be spending that kind of money to get it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A new Cyberpunk 2077 mod has overhauled Night City's rain, swapping the game's flat wet weather effects for individual 3D drops and adding lightning storms.

In a recent development, as spotted by DSOGaming, modder CyanideX's mod, Torrent, gives each raindrop its own size and falling speed. The drops also react to the player's movement, so they stream towards the windscreen when you're driving fast. If you find the wind has picked up, blustery weather can also push them sideways, too.

Sources indicate that the rain also catches the light from street lamps, neon signs, car headlights, and taillights, and won't fall through roofs or inside buildings. Drops splash on the ground, heavy rain leaves mist in the distance, and cars throw up spray from their tyres on wet roads.

The mod complements this with a newly introduced lightning system, with branching bolts that flash and flicker before fading, and that can arrive in bursts during heavier storms.

If you like a little lightning, the frequency of bolts can be adjusted across 10 levels, and with the AudioXL mod installed, thunder follows each strike, timed to how far away it landed.

For players sensitive to flashing lights, a Reduce Flashes option dims the lightning, replaces its flicker with a single slow glow, and halves the number of strikes.

Torrent supports Nova City 2 and other weather mods, and adds extra storm effects for Nova City 2 players, including mist that rolls through the streets with the wind. It’s available now on Nexus Mods.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 went on to smash records as the highest-rated game of all time on Metacritic in just one day – but sorting by user reviews now paints a very different picture.

It has been revealed that it all boils down to a "review bomb" of sorts, for those familiar with the term. If you're not, it looks like folks are leaving scathing scores of 0 and 1 without providing much reason aside from gripes with… well, what they perceive to be developers' political views (no, I will not elaborate further here – but they're all on Metacritic, free to read). There are some criticisms that Rockstar's game is console-exclusive here and there, too. That, and the game's 30 frame per second cap, of course. The GTA 6 review bomb isn't too surprising, though, all things considered – we are talking about the most hotly anticipated game of… well, ever. What is equal parts amusing and unfortunate, however, is that The Legend of Zelda fans are apparently catching strays over Nintendo's recent Ocarina of Time remake and its own score. Just have a look at its negative reviews on Metacritic. They're, uh, certainly something. "GTA 6," reads one, going on to slate Nintendo. Another just claims, "The game is too bad!!!" Further down, you'll find the assertion that "GTA 6 best." Others take things a step further and make their literal username on the website a variation of "GTA fan." Thankfully, these strange shots from the wilder side of the GTA 6 community aren't seeming to make much of a dent in Ocarina of Time's overall score.

It has dropped, though. Just a couple of days ago, its user score was 9.6 – right now, it sits at only 8.3. Again, it's nowhere near as bad as the GTA 6 rating at this moment, but it's still silly to see an entirely unrelated game hit with a review bomb (presumably because it's the other big November launch). I'd recommend keeping an eye on both Metacritic pages if you're curious about how things will continue to unfold… I know I certainly am.

Barbie Rewind, out now, invites you to take a trip down memory lane with a whole bunch of life in plastic classics, and one game that was previously unreleased

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (357 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Is there a character not originally from a video game that has more games than Barbie?
  • The latest release from Digital Eclipse, aficionados of digital multi-pack games like Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration and last year's Mortal Kombat: Legacy Kollection, Barbie Rewind has a total of 16 games from across the doll's video game history.
  • Beyond that, there's the customizable DreamHouse, where you get a whole bunch of furniture to deck it out with.

Is there a character not originally from a video game that has more games than Barbie? Maybe! I don't want to do any maths right now, but there aren't many that could touch her on sheer numbers. She's had all sorts of digital adventures, her games having a huge influence on the world of 'girl games'. As complicatedly gendered that may now be, the significance can't be understated, and as of today you can have a romp through a nice portion of that history in Barbie Rewind, a compilation of almost two decades worth of games all wrapped up in a nice little decorating game.

The latest release from Digital Eclipse, aficionados of digital multi-pack games like Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration and last year's Mortal Kombat: Legacy Kollection, Barbie Rewind has a total of 16 games from across the doll's video game history. Starting all the way back in 1991 with Barbie for the original NES, it jumps around to the Game Boy Color with Barbie: Pet Rescue, to the SNES with Barbie: Vacation Adventure. That last one's key because it's actually an unreleased game, making it quite a neat addition to the package.

Beyond that, there's the customizable DreamHouse, where you get a whole bunch of furniture to deck it out with. Nothing overly complicated here, it's just a thematically appropriate appendage that helps to recreate the feeling of playing with a doll house in pixel art form. Expect familiar faces like Ken, Teresa and Christie to pop up here and there as well. You'll also find a digital lookbook where you can "flip through the pages of Barbie history.".

Industry observers note that perhaps slightly disappointingly you won't find a number of beloved Barbie games like Barbie: Secret Agent or Barbie Horse Adventures: Mystery Ride. A lot of the games in this package are the 2D, pixel art entries, so that was probably meant to be the focus here. Hopefully someone will part those 3D releases somewhere down the line! In any case, if you fancy a trip down memory lane, you can pick up Barbie Rewind on Steam now.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One former Rockstar Games lead has a revolutionary take about GTA 6 – "it is good." But even though that may be the case, he reckons that "the complaints are real" in Chapter 1 from those suggesting that it "doesn't feel like a sandbox" and instead feels like a "girlfriend simulator.".

Obbe Vermeij worked at Rockstar Games between 1995 and 2009, serving as technical director on GTA 3, 4, Vice City, and San Andreas. Obviously, he'd left the studio well before GTA 6 started development (it might have been a long time coming, but it wasn't that long), so he's been playing through it alongside the rest of us.

Recent findings suggest that "It is good. Very good," he begins in a post on Twitter. However, there's a "but" coming.

Recent findings suggest that "In chapter 1 (The first 8 hours or so) the game doesn't give you much choice," he continues. "There are many tutorials, cut scenes, mandatory missions and the missions are basic. The complaints are real (realism over gameplay, girlfriend simulator, doesn't feel like a sandbox).".

Industry observers note that opinions here do vary – I've definitely seen more than a few social media posts complaining about the optional tasks of grocery shopping for Lucia and buying her flowers, for example. They probably weren't high up the list of activities fans who planned to enter Leonida and immediately commit heinous crimes had in mind, I suppose – though it's worth keeping in mind that, again, those parts are optional.

Sources indicate that equally, though, I've seen plenty of people enjoying the almost life-sim-esque vibe of GTA 6's opening hours, and that's probably reflected in how much time people spend in that first chapter. As someone who spent 18 hours in Chapter 1, you can probably guess what camp I fall into.

Regardless, though, Vermeij reckons things really pick up by the time you reach the second chapter. "In chapter 2, the game backs off and gives you a bunch of missions to choose from," he says. "This is when the GTA magic kicks in.".

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

Vermeij indicates he's now 46% of the way through the story in Chapter 3 and "having loads of fun now." He concludes that the "production values are unreal," and I don't think anyone could disagree with that.

Recent findings suggest that GTA 6 reviews have been glowing across the board, and Rockstar has already achieved almost unfathomable commercial success, with a whopping 32.5 million copies sold via pre-orders (eclipsing a figure that took Elden Ring three years to reach) and earning $3.79 billion on day one. It had the biggest entertainment launch in history – I don't think the devs could have hoped for anything better.

Police have arrested a suspect after a drive-by shooting at an office campus in Tustin, California, which is home to Xbox-owned studio inXile Entertainment.

According to Aftermath, officers responded to reports of a drive-by shooting at Flight at Tustin Legacy, a campus that houses inXile and other businesses, on 11th November.

Sources indicate that "Located multiple shell casings. Nobody was hurt," Tustin Police Sergeant Christopher Peterson told the outlet. "Processed the crime scene, and then sometime [Friday] morning, a little before 11 [AM], they took a suspect into custody. And the investigation is still kind of ongoing as to where and why.".

According to recent reports, "We're relieved that no one was hurt at our inXile office," an inXile spokesperson remarked. "Our focus is on supporting our team, and we are working closely with law enforcement as they investigate.".

Police have not given a motive, and the suspect has not been named.

InXile is the studio behind the Wasteland series, and is right now working on Clockwork Revolution.

Recent findings suggest that I often find it quite dull that the main takeaway far too many people have taken from Dark Souls, aside from thinking that the most interesting thing is its combat, is that it's all so bloomin' grimdark. I'm not saying I need sunshine and rainbows, I'd just like a vibe that's even remotely trying to be different from FromSoftware's seminal work. And so! I am quite pleased to discover MycoRelic, a Soulslike that pits you as a robot that covers its body in mushroom parts that offer elemental powers.

MycoRelic, from the offset, has this low-poly style that almost reminds me of oldschool RuneScape in a way I clown with quite promptly. The game looks good! The vibes look odd and, thankfully, not particularly derivative of medieval aesthetics. But while I am vibes-first when it comes to games, a Soulslike does live and die by its systems, and the systems here sound quite intriguing.

Recent findings suggest that for starters, there are no classes to speak of, just various weapons with their own moves and stats, and armour that "suits your playstyle and aesthetic." Huzzah! A game that understands one of the best bits of Dark Souls is dressing up. When you start out, you just have a "decrepit, moldy frame," but over time you can replace parts of it to improve your health, stamina, frame integrity, and the "potency of your fungal magic." Mycellic music to my ears.

It has been revealed that different fungi have different powers, and can be combined to create upcoming effects, or used in a multitude of ways; healing water can restore your friends or put out a fire for example. And oh, yes, there's co-op too, though I don't know if it's the friction-heavy Dark Souls kind or the seamless, hassle-free kind. On top of all this you've got an air-dash and can glide too, offering up some tasty platforming potential not typically found in the genre. I like it! And it just came out in 1.0 after a period of early access. If you fancy giving it a go, there's still a demo on Steam, or you can just pick up the full thing.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Thanks to a meaty, well-produced Diablo 4 Developer Upgrade, we got to have our promised first look at gameplay of the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.
  • The showcase offered a deep look at the Warlock’s core archetypes, its gameplay and skills loop, and where the class sits within the game’s existing roster of diverse classes.
  • Sources indicate that since the initial reveal of Lord of Hatred, The Warlock has remained the mysterious second class.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Thanks to a meaty, well-produced Diablo 4 Developer Upgrade, we got to have our promised first look at gameplay of the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

The showcase offered a deep look at the Warlock’s core archetypes, its gameplay and skills loop, and where the class sits within the game’s existing roster of diverse classes.

Sources indicate that since the initial reveal of Lord of Hatred, The Warlock has remained the mysterious second class. Anyone who pre-purchased the expansion was able to get immediate access to The Paladin, the other class arriving with the expansion. It wasn’t until February that Blizzard officially revealed the class to the world, but we had to wait until this most recent Developer Update to actually see it in action.

According to recent reports, the Warlock’s pragmatism exists as the counterpart to The Paladin's purity, in that Warlocks don’t shy away from harnessing the powers of Hell to eliminate their enemies. The class can conjure up demons to do their bidding, and utilise attacks previously only available to legions of Hell.

Sources indicate that the Warlock is a hybrid pet and caster class. Their gameplay revolves around summoning demons, and undermining enemies with shadow arts. They rely on two resources: Wrath, and Dominance. Casting Skills consumes Wrath, whereas Dominance is what allows the Warlock to summon and exploit demons.

The Warlock has four archetypes players can spec into. Legions are traditional summoners who rely on overwhelming numbers to crush enemies. Vanguards are closer to Sorcerers, capable of dealing damage head-on. Masterminds utilise shadowcraft to slowly drain their enemies. Finally, Ritualists are summoners of the most terrifying Hell demons.

In a recent development, the Warlock is able to do this by fusing Soul Shards into their bodies. Going down any of the four paths becomes available after reaching level 30, which is when the class mechanic is unlocked. Each Soul Shard is tied to a certain demon, and its through that power that the Warlock is able to call upon them in combat. Your choice does, of course, affect your abilities going forward.

Warlocks arrive alongside latest Uniques that cater to their specific playstyles, which is similar to what we’ve previously seen with The Paladin, and The Spiritborn before that.

Lord of Hatred arrives April 28. While we wait, Diablo 4’s next season is kicking off next week to deliver a bit of mindless fun to hold us over until the major day.

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (400 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • EA has made some notable leadership changes within its studios group, and in who oversees the Battlefield franchise.
  • Beede confirmed the change on LinkedIn, saying that he now oversees EA's shooter and action-RPG portfolio, seemingly occupying the role of the late Vince Zampella.
  • According to recent reports, in this stead, EA appointed Sam Cooper as Battlefield's newly introduced boss.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

EA has made some notable leadership changes within its studios group, and in who oversees the Battlefield franchise. Byron Beede, previously Battlefield's general manager, has been promoted to group general manager.

Beede confirmed the change on LinkedIn, saying that he now oversees EA's shooter and action-RPG portfolio, seemingly occupying the role of the late Vince Zampella.

According to recent reports, in this stead, EA appointed Sam Cooper as Battlefield's newly introduced boss. Cooper, who also revealed his new job title on LinkedIn, previously had a stint at EA Sports, but he's mostly known for his work at Activision, where he spent the last five-ish years as Call of Duty's global product management and head of live service.

While this might seem like fairly unremarkable corporate news - executives move between rival companies all the time, after all - it reinforces a narrative that EA continues to keenly replicate Activision's Call of Duty model.

That particular push is years-old now, and it kicked off in 2021 when EA hired Byron Beede, former boss of all of Call of Duty at Activision, to lead the next evolution of Battlefield. So far, that decision has given us the very successful Battlefield 6 and its free-to-play, COD: Warzone-like battle royale mode Redsec.

In a recent development, to facilitate that, EA rearranged several of its studios to serve under one banner dubbed Battlefield Studios, replicating Activision's model of locking several teams around the world into developing and supporting a single game / franchise. Ripple Effect, Motive, the iconic Criterion and, of course, series creator DICE are all the Battlefield franchise's lead and support studios.

Sources indicate that many players argue - and I would agree - that Battlefield and Call of Duty games are more alike today than they've ever been. The user interface, the emphasis on limited-time events, the garish store cosmetics, the COD-like battle pass system - complete with a more expensive option, are all signs of that transition. And that is to say nothing of controversial changes to longstanding Battlefield tenets, such as the class system, intended to make Battlefield 6 appeal to a wider audience.

The effects of that leadership change likely won't materialise until the next Battlefield title, but it's a curious one to keep in mind as EA leans even harder into its biggest franchises following its $55bn private equity and Saudi Arabia's PIF-funded buyout.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The good (and hilarious) folks over at HDTVTest have been looking at the HDR Calibration settings for GTA 6 on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, and they've discovered that the tool is actually slightly broken as things stand.

Some of the specifics go over my head a little bit to be honest, but in a nutshell, the figures that are displayed on the calibration tool don't fully translate into the game itself, leading to a potentially inoptimal picture.

As a result, they've published a new nine-minute video (which you can see up above) to explain the problems.

According to recent reports, "The HDR calibration screen in GTA 6 can be misleading, because Rockstar's Max Brightness, Paper White and Black Levels settings interact in unexpected ways. To be clear, GTA VI's HDR rendering isn't broken… it's the calibration procedure that can give misleading results.".

The video goes step-by-step on how they analysed the complications and tried to figure out the best possible HDR settings for GTA 6, and while their tests aren't fully concluded yet (there's another video to come in the future where they try multiple consumer displays), they've shared their initial best settings for displays capable of 1,000 nits or brighter.

Here are those three settings, but again, keep in mind that your TV must be capable of 1,000 nits of brightness or more, and that certain smart TV features or special HDR settings on your TV itself may interfere with the results.

Industry observers note that if your display isn't capable of 1,000 nits, do a bit of Googling to try and find out the specifics for your TV/monitor, and then times that figure by two in-game. So, if you're working with a maximum of 600 nits, set the figure as 1,200.

I have to be honest and say I'm not seeing a lot of difference here, but I've also got an old TV with a max brightness of just over 600 nits, not to mention I'm using a few image-altering features that may be playing havoc with the settings. It's also noted in the video that this is generally based on playing in the dark, rather than in a brightly-lit room.

According to recent reports, have a play for yourself and see what you think - there's clearly a lot of people who are very thankful for these settings on YouTube and beyond, so we wanted to at least make you aware of them. The reality is that you may need to still do a bit of tweaking to find the perfect sweet spot for your setup though.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • We’d rightly criticise Sony if the PS5 had fallen to pieces during GTA 6’s launch, so let’s give the platform holder a nod of approval for navigating these past two weeks almost flawlessly.
  • Sources indicate that there were some minor scattered instances of PSN outages on Wednesday evening prior to the Rockstar title’s significant launch, but these never affected everyone and the network recovered pretty fast.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We’d rightly criticise Sony if the PS5 had fallen to pieces during GTA 6’s launch, so let’s give the platform holder a nod of approval for navigating these past two weeks almost flawlessly.

Sources indicate that there were some minor scattered instances of PSN outages on Wednesday evening prior to the Rockstar title’s significant launch, but these never affected everyone and the network recovered pretty fast. I think we can give that a pass.

Meanwhile, the preload process worked flawlessly as far as I’m aware. I haven’t really seen any widespread reporting of people being unable to download the game in advance of its release.

Given its size and the sheer number of people wanting to play – remember, 32.5 million copies were sold across all consoles prior to release – that’s a humongous strain on Sony’s servers, which is predicted to have accounted for approximately 75% of all purchases.

Obviously GTA 6 is a single player-only game, so that certainly put less stress on the PSN as a whole, and the new GTA Online’s eventual launch will be an even bigger test – but for now, the PS5 has held up remarkably well.

I’m not saying we should get out the champagne – this is the experience consumers quite rightly expect Sony to deliver.

But this was still a huge, unprecedented test for PlayStation’s infrastructure – and it’s fair to say it navigated it almost flawlessly. In my opinion, that deserves acknowledging at least.

Hark! A newly introduced Slay the Spire 2 patch is here! Or, well, it is if you're someone who's trying out the beta branches of the game. If you're not, it might be worth trying out, as Mega Crit say this is their biggest patch for the game so far, with "some really impactful bits of content that will require lots of testing before they reach the main branch.".

It has been revealed that first up, a upcoming character: The Fool! "Wah!! The first new character for Early Access arrives!" a Steam blog post explains. "A silly musician who wields a bow! How can such a whimsical creature survive within the Spire? Why, that's up to you! We expect to make a great number of content and balance changes before the Fool is ready for the main branch. Even more importantly, be sure to have fun figuring out all the strategies and story of this gently bard. It would be foolish not to!" The post doesn't go into much detail as to what the new character can actually do, so, you'll have to discover that one for yourself!

Industry observers note that there are also two new game modes to try out with this beta patch. The first is Blitz, a "condensed and chaotic deckbuilding-focused mode." Here, the "Merchant's wares feel a bit off, the map is gone, and Gold no longer matters." You'll also find it comes with five levels of Ascension shared across every character, and you can unlock it by completing an Ascension run on any difficulty. The second mode is Dread, which as the name implies, is a "brutal" difficulty mode that you can only play if you've reached Ascension 10 on every character, including The Fool. "All ascension modifiers are enabled. Bosses are stronger and buff all enemies in their Act. Curses will also pile up as you climb the Spire. Death is expected.".

You can expect a bunch of latest balance tweaks and changes too. For starters, you'll find that rest sites can now appear a floor earlier every act. New events have been added to Underdocks and Act 2 and 3 too. Some nice quality of life alterations have been made, like how the character select screen for standard runs will start on whatever character you played as last, and controller navigation at the Merchant has been improved too. Industry observers note that after a couple of delays, a plagiarism lawsuit, and at least one internal reboot, Bungie’s next major game has officially introduced. Marathon, the extraction shooter from the studio behind Destiny, has managed to find a decent, if a little small of an audience.

The game’s player numbers on Steam are being compared to its recent free, open weekend, and not in a favourable manner.

Prior to Marathon’s launch, Bungie held a multi-day Server Slam, which offered anyone interested in playing the game a chance to try out almost all of its classes, two of its maps, as well as many of its gameplay and progression systems.

The open test was largely well-received, and players actually showed up for it. It peaked at a very respectable 143,621 concurrent players on Steam, which put it within striking distance of the peak concurrent of its chief competitor, Arc Raiders - at least when you compare both of their pre-launch Server Slam events.

In Arc Raiders’ case, those figures were far outpaced at the game’s actual launch, and the Embark shooter continues to command a very active player base to this day. A paid product garnering far more players than the same product’s own free sampler is never not a good sign, so many hoped something similar would happen with Marathon.

Marathon has now officially launched, and it doesn’t look like it managed to pull an Arc Raiders - at least so far. At its peak, the Bungie shooter attracted 88,337 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), which is a little over half of its Server Slam’s 143,621 peak concurrent.

Numbers have, of course, dropped since then, which is normal, as players log off for the night. This is obviously not the end of the road for Marathon. Friday, and the weekend, may well push numbers closer to the Server Slam heights.

According to recent reports, indeed, word of mouth is quite positive, with the game at the moment sitting at a Very Positive user review rating on Steam, based on over 4,600 reviews. As has been proven time and time again in recent years, nothing catapults a game like players emphatically advocating for it to their friends, so it could simply be that mainstream players are cautious.

It will become clear where things settle over the weekend.

However, he also claims that the experience Cyberagent has gained with its major releases to date have allowed the organization to gain a clearer perspective on profitability and sustainability.

Sources indicate that this presentation comes after a notable month for Cygmes and Umamusume: Pretty Derby. The developer issued refunds for hotels and flights following the sudden cancellation of an LA live show for the game last month, then shortly after became a major sponsor of the Japanese Formula 1 Grand Prix. The game was also temporarily taken offline due to the major PHP vulnerability exposed last month, an outage that was thankfully short-lived.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Team Ninja continues to work on Nioh 3. The developer has been releasing regular updates for the action RPG since its launch in early February. Earlier patches have addressed major bugs like healing item use inconsistencies, and more have arrived since to tackle various balance and loot-related issues.

Today’s patch, version 1.04, is a major one, coming in at well over 1GB. There’s plenty here worth getting excited about, so let’s dig in.

To begin with, this is the patch that adds the promised free armour sets for both Ninja, and Samurai. When Nioh 3 reached one million sales, Team Ninja remarked it would gift every player the Thunderous set in celebration, and the set’s two variants are now available in-game.

Recent findings suggest that the more interesting side of the patch is, unsurprisingly, its change log. There appears to be a focus on online co-op and AI summons in this one, with various tweaks to the make the process more rewarding, and, in some cases, worthwhile.

In a recent development, the amount of Glory obtained when you complete a mission in multiplayer has been increased, regardless of which player was the host. The other major change mainly affects AI Benevolent Grave summons, making it so bosses will no longer target a single player for almost the entirety of the fight.

While summoning AI helpers has always been useful in Nioh 3, they didn’t always help in boss fights, specifically because the boss tended to focus on the player who summoned them, leaving the AI to run around eating AoE hits before dying.

Industry observers note that patch 1.04 makes a couple of welcome gameplay tweaks to the feel of combat. Ninjutsu, and Onmyo Magic will now hit their targets more consistently in situations where there’s a difference in elevation between the player and the enemy.

Sources indicate that in the same vein, you’ll now be able to attack (quick/strong) right after jumping, which removes the pause that previously buffered the attack instead. This could mean even more air combos that don’t specifically require Martial Arts.

You can look forward to a couple of quality of life tweaks in this patch, too, such as the change that allows the game to automatically send any Sudama Soul Cores dropped by merchants to your item box. This happens from the second one onwards, which means you won’t have to pick half a dozen each time you go to sell a batch of items.

Sources indicate that speaking of the item box, the limit of forging materials has been increased for some of them. If you’ve been running Battle Scroll missions and Expeditions for gear, you’ll be happy to know that you can now exit the session from the main menu directly.

According to recent reports, there’s plenty more to patch 1.04, including fixes and balance tweaks for several weapons, such as Samurai dual swords, odachi, and more for a few Ninja weapons, too. The patch also brings several bug fixes to the game.

You can read the full set of patch notes on Steam.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The director of Marvel's scrapped Blade movie, Bassam Tariq, has reflected candidly on his time working on the movie.

The film was set to star Mahershala Ali as the titular vampire hunter, but it never actually made its way to screens.

It has been revealed that "It was funny and strange to start casting and building without a proper script. You're sitting there and explaining to actors what their role will be, and they just have to believe you," he told The Newly introduced Arab, when asked what his time in the studio system taught him.

Recent findings suggest that "That's also very dangerous because if the text comes and it doesn't add up to what you were saying, your credibility gets completely shot," he continued. "All I have is my integrity, and I've been thinking about that a lot.

In a recent development, "If you're the bearer of bad news to your actors, but you're not the one making any of these decisions – and it's actually coming from a corporate entity – that's not a great way to be a director," he shared. "I know some people can take that and run with it, but I learned I was losing credibility with my actors, and it wasn't a healthy way to operate as a filmmaker.".

Then, Tariq got even franker about the experience. "Life's too short to make shit films, so that was my substantial lesson: I have to have full control over my script," he said. "If we disagree, it's between them and me. It's quite sad because we had such high hopes for what we wanted to build.".

However, he added that he was pleased Ryan Coogler's Sinners was able to make use of Ruth E. Carter's costumes, because that film "feels so much bolder than what we could have accomplished.".

Ali has also been very upfront about his thoughts on the movie failing to materialize. "That's a Kevin Feige question," he said when asked why the film didn't happen. "They had, as you said, a two-time Oscar winning actor under contract, and you got billions of dollars. That's a question for them, why it didn't happen. I don't mean anything personal to you, but I don't know why it did. To this day, I don't know why it didn't happen. I just know that Kevin said it was the biggest failure of his career, and I agree.".

Next up for Marvel is Avengers: Doomsday, which brings together a supersized cast that includes Chris Hemsworth's Thor, Anthony Mackie's Captain America, the Fantastic Four, the Thunderbolts, and more.

It has been revealed that doomsday arrives this December 18. While you wait, check out our guide to all the upcoming Marvel movies and TV demonstrates for everything else that's on the way.

The next Xbox, Project Helix, is a console and "not a PC" claims Microsoft, as it clarifies that computational power isn't sole focus this time

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (868 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Microsoft has stressed that its next-generation Xbox console, Project Helix, "is not a PC that can also play console games", but rather "a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC".
  • The details come from a Microsoft-produced Xbox magazine made available digitally yesterday, and a Helix-related feature speaking to Xbox vice president of next generation, Jason Ronald.
  • "We're very clear on the design goal," Ronald later added.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Microsoft has stressed that its next-generation Xbox console, Project Helix, "is not a PC that can also play console games", but rather "a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC". The manufacturer has also underlined the importance of using gen-AI-adjacent "neural rendering" technology going forwards, and a desire to remove "all the barriers of play that have historically existed" - notably in making the past generations of games playable.

The details come from a Microsoft-produced Xbox magazine made available digitally yesterday, and a Helix-related feature speaking to Xbox vice president of next generation, Jason Ronald. "When we think about Project Helix, it's really designed to be the ultimate gaming machine," Ronald said, "one that removes all the barriers of play that have historically existed. My entire library is accessible to me. I'm able to bring four generations of my Xbox library and progression with me and have it available instantly. And we remove the arbitrary constraints between console and PC games.

"We're very clear on the design goal," Ronald later added. "Helix is designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC. It is not a PC that can also play console games. The goal is making it easy, intuitive, and instant to access my games. But if you're a hardcore gamer or a power user who wants to have that deeper level of customisability across settings and performance options, you can absolutely go do it.".

Recent findings suggest that notably, Ronald seemed to suggest that Helix - the console, not the handheld; "Helix" refers to a couple of machines - isn't solely focused on computational grunt. Indeed, he said the next generation wasn't about hitting 8K resolutions and 240 hertz frame-rates, but instead leaning on technologies like "neural rendering" - i.e. generative-AI - and encouraging innovation.

Industry observers note that "It's about deeper immersion," Ronald remarked. "It is about leveraging latest technical advancements such as neural rendering to deliver a new level of visual fidelity in more efficient and innovative ways. It's about new kinds of games and new game experiences that we haven't been able to do before. What excites me about the future is the idea of entirely new types of games that have never been possible before, delivered through all the innovation in the silicon and the hardware and the platform that we're delivering.".

Industry observers note that while referencing the global component shortage and exorbitant prices of computer hardware, he added: "This is a big reason why we're really focused on advancements like neural rendering because it's an entirely upcoming way to generate a frame without requiring more computational horsepower, additional memory, and things like that. I think you're going to see more innovation over the next three to five years than you've seen in the last 10 years.".

Xbox boss Asha Sharma also recently talked up the importance of generative-AI-sounding technology in Xbox's future, saying "too many ideas never become games", and that "a single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations".

According to recent reports, another key part of Xbox's Helix vision is compatibility and game preservation. "Game preservation is core to Xbox," Ronald went as far as to say. "Not only do we feel like it's the right thing for the industry, we feel a deep responsibility as one of its biggest platforms and publishers. For the first 30 years of game development, nobody really thought about game preservation when they were designing their hardware, when they were building their games." Xbox is apparently working with game-makers to ensure games can not only be played now but also 20 to 30 years into the future.

Recent findings suggest that the other key facet of Microsoft's push the familiar Play Anywhere mantra, whereby one game can be played across multiple devices, maintaining your game-progress as you go. This is fundamental to Microsoft's handheld-and-console Helix plan, and something we've seen the organization dry-run with the Xbox ROG Ally X handheld. "It's this notion that not only does my library move with me, but my progress moves with me as well," Ronald stated. "Because I fully expect that when I'm in the middle of an 80-hour RPG, if I'm 25 hours into that and I want to play it on another device, I should be able to instantly resume from where I was. Those are things that today are becoming more common, but I think in the future it's going to be a baseline expectation of all players.".

In a recent development, ronald wouldn't be drawn on the concern of price regarding Project Helix - a recent report suggested Helix could be priced up to $1800 - referring to it only as both "a challenging time" but an "exciting one", because "we have to invent entirely upcoming technology to continue to advance the state-of-the-art while also continuing to make things accessible and affordable". Ronald also wouldn't reference a release date, though the report referenced above suggested the handheld Helix machine will release next holiday, 2027, and the console Helix machine the year after. The next generation, then, seems to be around the corner.

While GTA 6 has been receiving unbelievable praise and is technically considered one of the best video games of all time according to Metacritic, that certainly doesn't mean it's immune to criticism.

Industry observers note that one of the major talking points both before and after launch has been that it's a 30FPS experience across all Xbox and PlayStation consoles, and if you're going from 60FPS back to 30FPS, there's definitely an adjustment period. Some people are absolutely fine with that, while others are finding it extremely difficult to go back.

For what it's worth, our friends at Digital Foundry have been analysing this in depth today:.

Rockstar Games has already confirmed recently that even the PS5 Pro doesn't come close to running GTA 6 at 60FPS due to the system's processor not being powerful enough, so we might be forced to wait until the next generation of consoles (and PC) before the game will become playable at 60 frames per-second.

"The PS5 Pro features an upgraded graphics processor and upscaling technology that we leverage to increase the game’s visual fidelity. While the PS5 Pro’s central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it is not powerful enough to run the game’s complex simulation at higher frame rates.”.

It has been revealed that with all of this in mind, we're interested to hear what you think about playing games at 30FPS on Xbox, PlayStation or anywhere else. It's becoming much more common that 60FPS is the default these days, but there are still some phenomenal 30FPS-only experiences out there, and it's a shame to think people are missing out on them.

I personally much prefer playing at 60FPS if I can, and there are certain games I will avoid at 30FPS until they get a patch down the line (like Mafia: Definitive Edition), but when it comes to industry-defining masterpieces like Red Dead Redemption 2 and Grand Theft Auto VI, the last thing I'd want is for them to scale back the detail in order to squeeze in a 60FPS mode.

Industry observers note that so, what do you think? Tell us in the poll above and in the comments section below.

Exclusive – Behind The Romance: Rockstar Talks GTAVI’s Jason And Lucia

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1588 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gameinformer

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that after dozens of hours exploring Leonida, I have a lot of positive things to say about Grand Theft Auto VI, and shared as much in our review of the game.
  • We reached out to senior members of the Rockstar Games team to ask about their thoughts on Jason and Lucia, and this is what they had to share.
  • Industry observers note that during my playthrough, the Jason and Lucia dynamic really elevated the experience, adding heart and emotional weight to the expected mix of action, driving, and activities around Leonida.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that after dozens of hours exploring Leonida, I have a lot of positive things to say about Grand Theft Auto VI, and shared as much in our review of the game. But for my part, the feature that elevated the game most prominently above Rockstar Games’ other (excellent) games wasn’t its graphics, missions, or action – it was the storytelling and interplay between the two lead protagonists. Jason and Lucia bring heart, emotional depth, and a sense of genuine threat to the crime fantasy, as you grow attached to them and start cheering for them against all the odds stacked against them.

We reached out to senior members of the Rockstar Games team to ask about their thoughts on Jason and Lucia, and this is what they had to share.

Industry observers note that during my playthrough, the Jason and Lucia dynamic really elevated the experience, adding heart and emotional weight to the expected mix of action, driving, and activities around Leonida. Was a couple or romantic relationship the plan or goal for the game from very early on in development, or did that come later? Do you see the focus on Jason and Lucia’s relationship as one of the features that separates Grand Theft Auto VI from your prior work on storytelling in the game series?

Sources indicate that stephen Donkin, Vice President of Design: “The dual protagonists and the relationship between the two of them was there from very early in development, but exactly how that was expressed in the game did change over time. It was an enormous challenge for us to get them working together in the open world together and finding exactly how that would work. As we started to layer in more mechanics, dialogue, and incremental features across all teams, it just clicked at some point. The ability to be together in the open world also allowed us for newly introduced ways to tell the story of the game and to bring some of the exposition and narrative into the open world in a way we hadn’t been able to do before. Hearing these little bits of dialogue as you are just tooling around the world that have specific context to what you as a player have just been doing in the story really knits it all together.”.

In a recent development, the player has a choice for how to develop the relationship between the two leads, but I imagine most players are drawn toward helping it thrive. In early playtests, is that what you observed?

Katie Pica, Design Director: Player Systems & Progression:“Overall, we’ve seen that players are invested in supporting Jason and Lucia’s relationship but we don’t favor a specific path through the game, it is completely down to player choice.”.

Sources indicate that it feels like a lot of the game’s driving narrative beats factor for a close connection between Jason and Lucia. Was it challenging to craft variations that included a more tense or distant connection between the two? Is that even possible?

Luke Howard, Senior Design Director: Missions & Visualization:“One of the core goals of this game was to tell the story of Jason and Lucia with a base line relationship where they are amicable, if just platonic, as they still share the same ultimate goals and need each other to achieve them. So, this gave us a good platform on the main flow to expand particularly intense or emotional moments they experience with variation that can expand on their romantic relationship, while not losing anything if that doesn’t exist. In short, we did develop variation in scenes and interactions that range from subtle to more significant, but done in a way that should feel authentic to the player’s choices, relationship-wise and also criminal profile.

In a recent development, one example is after Lucia helps Kordell’s gang pull off an intense armored truck robbery she shares the information with Raul’s crew. Afterwards Jason pulls Lucia aside to see how she's coping. This moment carries several variations where the performance direction was captured multiple ways to cover a range emotional energy between them. The actors deliveries are brilliant and nuanced – these small tender moments are where we tried to craft pieces that when added up together over the course of the story, author an authentic version of the player’s Jason and Lucia.”.

Were there any fictional couples or real-life couples that the team looked at for inspiration in shaping the Jason and Lucia dynamic, whether those couples came from major crime stories or not?

It has been revealed that rupert Humphries, Senior Vice President of Narrative:“We definitely started by looking at all the “couple on the run” movies. There are a lot of them but the ones that we kept coming back to were Warren Beatty and Faye Dunaway in Bonnie and Clyde, McQueen and MacGraw in The Getaway (the Jim Thomson book is also great), True Romance, Thelma and Louise. Clooney and JLo’s dynamic in Out of Sight, as well. And then a lot of buddy movies actually – Riggs and Murtaugh, Butch and Sundance, Mike Lowry and Marcus Burnett, etc. for their back and forth together. In terms of having a game where the characters can change based on how you play and whether you really lean into and enjoy the crime spree we thought about how both Pulp Fiction and Natural Born Killers start with a couple in a diner pulling out guns, but then how different those couples are and how different those scenarios play out. Jason and Lucia are a lot tougher than Tim Roth and Amanda Plummer but we liked the idea of telling a story where Jason and Lucia could end up being closer to either end of that spectrum based on what the player was doing.”.

Sex and intimacy are notoriously complicated and challenging to present in games. How did you aim to strike a balance with their private moments together that felt authentic? Any thoughts about how or why it’s so challenging to present adult relationships in video games?

Recent findings suggest that rupert Humphries, Senior Vice President of Narrative:“This is definitely something we thought a lot about and spent a long time trying to get right. The actors who play Jason and Lucia were so good, and they had a natural chemistry and part of it was just trying to capture some of that.

According to recent reports, there’s this trade off in making games between player control and then scripted scenarios. We try and give the player as much control as we can because we are working in an interactive medium and actually doing something rather than watching it is going to feel more powerful. But then you have the ability to really mess around and break the illusion of a tender or romantic moment or whatever it is. So the relationship aspect of this story is there if a player wants to engage in it, but if they don’t the story can play out differently.”.

Sources indicate that in its best moments of genuine support, regular connection, open communication, and flirty or engagement with one another, Jason and Lucia can come across as a pretty ideal model of good relationships – even while they’re simultaneously committing major crimes together. Was that juxtaposition of a healthy romantic relationship against an external world of illicit activity an explicit goal for how the narrative came together?

Rupert Humphries, Senior Vice President of Narrative:“That was the goal, yes. You are really living with these characters – they’re eating, sleeping, showering, throwing away their trash, or not. The relationship needed to feel real to sit alongside all of that. Then even just as a development team, we live with these characters for years and years. We wanted them to be people we could like, care about, and root for. And they needed to like each other. But then the world itself is so crazy and chaotic and seemingly on the brink of collapse.

Recent findings suggest that when we set out to make this game, and go into that multiyear development marathon, we remarked we wanted to spend our time working on something with heart, and with some characters you could care about and root for. It’s barely worth even stating, but we are living in a time when people are divided along almost every line, and feelings about the future are pretty bleak. We wanted to create a world that held up a mirror to that, showed that fever pitch of craziness that we are all maybe a couple of bad decisions away from, but we wanted the story we were going to tell to have something positive at its core and the message that human connection is better than division.”.

In a recent development, the game automatically moves you to play one character or another at certain points, but for many sequences, you can choose your playable lead. In your experience playing and watching others play, do most players gravitate toward one character or another as “their character?”.

According to recent reports, stephen Donkin, Vice President of Design:“It really varied in our playthroughs. They are both such great characters and performances that people seemed to gravitate to both of them in different ways. But overall, we have found the split of time between characters to be relatively even on a per-playthrough and also at a macro level.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Xbox have confirmed that Wolfenstein 3 is indeed in production at Indiana Jones and the Great Circle devs MachineGames and that Doom makers id Software have started work on their next game after losing a bunch of staff to the mass layoffs across Microsoft's gaming division this year.

In a recent development, "A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations," isn't part of the marketing spiel for either of those games. Instead, it's something Xbox CEO Asha Shama has bellowed amid a rant outlining how she sees the company's future.

The Wolfenstein and id confirmations came as Xbox had a bit of a social media party to commemorate their 25th birthday. Sharma, ever keen to be seen right next to any positive news coming out of the tech giant, confirmed Wolfenstein 3 is in production by posting a photo showing a few lines from its script. Around the same time, she shouted out Doom: The Dark Ages Revelations' incoming Slaughter Mode, adding that "the team is already working on its next game".

The official id Software account responded to note that this next game is being made by their "teams in Texas and Frankfurt, with game direction once again by Hugo Martin", and that "it'll be some time before [they're] ready to share more".

We're incredibly excited about our next project, a new game from our teams in Texas and Frankfurt, with game direction once again by Hugo Martin. It'll be some time before we're ready to share more but we can't wait for you to see what we're working on.

Alongside hollering about these couple of games, Sharma put out a 25th anniversary statement which for the most part does the sort of bigging up of Xbox's past you'd expect. Good times were had, we blazed a trail and made lots of money, etcetera. The final section saw the exec attempt to look forward to the next 25 years for Xbox.

"While modern games demonstrate the heights of human craft in ways unimaginable just decades ago, the cost, resources, and risk required to create them have grown just as dramatically," she wrote. "As a result, too many ideas never become games, and too many games fall short of what their creators imagined. For decades, this has been the unavoidable tradeoff of ambition. We must change this.

"Throughout human history, the scale of what we could create was determined by the people, capital, and resources we could command. That relationship is beginning to break. A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations. A small team will be able to build worlds that today demand hundreds of developers and hundreds of millions of dollars. And our largest studios will be able to pursue ambitions as far beyond today's games as Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 is from its first entry in 1982.".

It has been revealed that that certainly sounds a lot like the sales pitch the biggest proponents of generative AI keep wheeling out, while avoiding saying generative AI out loud in the hopes of making it more palatable to folks who might not make the connection. I'm waiting for Sharma to put out another post revealing that she accidentally mixed another section of the Wolfenstein script into her celebratory musings, but I'm not holding my breath.

Xbox parent company Microsoft are still at the moment subject to a BDS movement boycott over their reported ties to the Israeli military.
